system.name: PipeThreader
system.one_liner: a DNN compiler that combines tile-based data parallelism with pipelined scheduling across heterogeneous GPU execution units

components.name: DFG of operators
components.role: example input data-flow graph of operators A and B

components.name: sTask partition
components.role: partitions each operator by configuring the TileShape of sTasks

components.name: sTask-graph
components.role: graph of sTasks preserving the computation and data dependencies of the original DFG

components.name: sTask scheduling
components.role: schedules sTasks across EUs and sEUs using a two-level (inter-EU, intra-EU) algorithm

components.name: Virtualized Device
components.role: two-layer hardware abstraction of the underlying accelerator that executes the sProgram

components.name: EU
components.role: homogeneous execution unit enabling SPMD-style parallelism across sTask-subgraphs

components.name: sEU
components.role: specialized execution unit within an EU supporting MPMD-style parallelism for heterogeneous hardware (e.g., TensorCores vs CUDA cores)

content.key_idea: PipeThreader compiles a DFG into an sTask-graph, schedules sTasks across heterogeneous execution units (EU/sEU) on a virtualized device, and uses runtime profiling to inform scheduling.
content.reading_order: Top-down: input DFG through sTask partition, sTask-graph, sTask scheduling, down into the virtualized device's EU/sEU units, with profiling feeding back up.

encoding.emphasis: The bold dark-gray process boxes (sTask partition, sTask scheduling) and the labelled transition arrows (sTask-graph, sProgram, Profiling) highlight PipeThreader's new compilation and scheduling stages, while colored A/B boxes trace how operators are transformed into sTasks and mapped onto sEUs

Our scheduling policy is inspired by the two-layer hardware abstraction described in Figure 3

summary: Figure 3 gives the system overview of PipeThreader, a DNN compiler that fuses tile-based data parallelism with pipelined scheduling for heterogeneous GPU execution units. The top-down diagram starts from an example DFG of operators A and B, which sTask-partition converts into an sTask-graph of fine-grained, dependency-preserving sTasks (shown as repeated blue-A/orange-B chains). sTask scheduling then applies a two-level algorithm to produce an sProgram, which runs on a Virtualized Device modeled as multiple EUs, each holding heterogeneous sEUs (e.g., TensorCore-like and CUDA-core-like units) that execute A/B sTasks in a defined order. A Profiling arrow feeds runtime measurements from the device back into sTask scheduling, closing the loop between compilation and execution.
